This premium version is the US-tree P-63A-5 with better reward modifiers, and it shares traits with Soviet fighters: a heavy cannon, a preference for low altitude and good agility. Unlike Yaks, though, it can survive dives approaching 900 km/h, although compression makes steep dives near the ground risky. It has been in the game since the open beta.
p-63c-5: When the Merlin-engined P-63B came to nothing, production moved to the P-63C, whose water-injected Allison reached about 1,800 hp; the wingspan was trimmed, and the C-5 added a ventral fin and more armour; over 1,000 were built, many going to the Soviet Union and around 100 to France. In the game its V-1710-117 makes it much stronger than the P-63A down low, but it is still weak at height, so low-altitude fights suit it best. Armament remains a 37 mm hub cannon and four 12.7 mm guns, plus three 500 lb bombs; the cannon's low-velocity AP rounds are a poor choice against armour. It has been available since the open beta.
p-63c-5_france: France took 114 Kingcobras near the war's end and from 1947 used them in Indochina as napalm-armed ground attackers, the Viet Minh having no aircraft, until anti-aircraft losses and surplus Hellcats, Bearcats and Corsairs ended their service. In the game it is an energy fighter and high-altitude interceptor that turns slightly better than earlier Kingcobras; its fast dive and good energy retention let it make repeated high yo-yo attacks on enemies below. Three 500 lb bombs give it some use in ground battles, and unlike the identical US version it can also carry incendiary bombs. It arrived in Update 1.73 "Vive la France".
p-63c-5_kingcobra_animal_version: This Kingcobra is a standard P-63C-5, the water-injected, ventral-finned development of the P-63A, wearing a fictional snakeskin finish rather than any historical scheme. It was a reward from the 2018 "Flying Serpent, Crouching Tiger" crafting event in Update 1.77 "Advancing Storm" and matches the tech-tree aircraft in performance and weapons. Its uprated Allison gives far more power than earlier Kingcobras, but many opponents still outclass it at altitude, so it fights best low down, where compression makes aggressive high-speed dives near the ground unwise.
p-63c-5_ussr: Of the 3,273 Kingcobras built between 1943 and 1945, roughly 2,400 went to the Soviet Union; the P-63C, 1,227 of them, had the stronger V-1710-117 engine and a slightly shorter span, and the C-5 added wing racks for two 500 lb bombs and a ventral fin for directional stability. This Soviet example was a reward from the 2016 "War Thunder Fulfills Your Wishes!" event. A fast climber with good agility and hard-hitting guns, it does well in air combat, particularly higher up, but its wing fuel tanks are easily hit and it bleeds speed in tight turns.
p-66: Vultee's P-66 Vanguard, designed for Sweden, was kept by the US after Pearl Harbor for defence and training and then sold in numbers to China, where the 3rd and 5th Air Groups used its speed for hit-and-run attacks on the nimbler Ki-43 and Ki-44 until P-40s replaced most in 1943. It looks a little like the P-36 but has a longer, rounder fuselage, narrower wings and a roomy canopy, a result of sharing parts with trainers. Balanced rather than outstanding, it lacks the CW-21's sparkle but is the first Chinese fighter able to absorb some damage, and it prepares pilots for the P-40E. It arrived in Update 1.91 "Night Vision".
p1y1_mod11: Requested by the Japanese Navy, whose G3M and G4M bombers could not dive-bomb, the Ginga was a fast land-based bomber whose long development ended with prototypes rushed into production, leaving it hard to maintain and few in number. In the game it is among the quickest bombers at its level, exceeding 675 km/h in a dive, and is flown like the Ju 288 C and Ar 234 B-2: dive, release, escape, repeat. Its airframe is flimsy, its defensive guns light and its belly unguarded, so it relies on speed, can out-turn heavier pursuers, and uses its rear gunner to throw off attackers' aim. It arrived in Update 1.63 "Desert Hunters".
p1y1_mod11_china: Japan based Ginga bombers at Tainan in 1944 to defend Taiwan, but they achieved little and were abandoned; the Nationalist air force flew 12 of them until American bombers took over in 1946, then scrapped them with hundreds of other Japanese aircraft to remove any risk of armed revolt. Added in Update 1.91 "Night Vision", it is a dive-and-run bomber like the Ju 288 and Ar 234, topping 675 km/h in a dive. Once slow and low it is very exposed, as its defensive guns are weak and its underside unguarded, but it outpaces most Japanese fighters except the J5N1, Ki-108 and J2M.
p_108a_serie2: The P.108A "Artigliere" was a gunship version of Piaggio's P.108 heavy bomber, built for a 1942 anti-shipping requirement around a 102 mm cannon with a 12-round autoloader, among the largest guns then fitted to an aircraft; only one prototype was built before cancellation in September 1943. In the game the gun, with 50 rounds, suits large ships rarely met outside Simulator Battles, and the slow, unwieldy airframe makes hitting vehicles, let alone aircraft, very hard. Sitting low in the tree, it is often flown as bait instead, luring careless fighters onto its defensive turrets, though an attacker who picks the right angle finds it an easy kill.
p_108b_serie1: The P.108B serie 1 is an Italian heavy bomber added in Update 1.69 "Regia Aeronautica". It carries a heavy bomb load but only light defensive armament, so it needs to bomb from high altitude and steer clear of fighting wherever possible. Bases, airfields and fixed targets such as pillboxes are its natural prey, with slow ships possible if the drop is timed well. Once an enemy fighter catches it, its gunners can buy time until help arrives but rarely score a kill.
p_108b_serie2: Added in Update 1.69 "Regia Aeronautica", the P.108B serie 2 is an Italian heavy bomber with a big bomb load, weak defences and a lot of fuel in its wings, which makes wing hits especially dangerous. It has no forward-firing guns, so attackers should be kept behind it, where the gunners can respond, though they rarely drive off a determined fighter. Its best defence is planning: a route around likely interceptors, high altitude, few turns and, ideally, a fighter escort, before hitting bases, airfields, pillboxes or slow ships.
pb4y-2: Consolidated's PB4Y-2 Privateer was a purpose-built naval Liberator to follow the converted PB4Y-1, with a stretched fuselage for a flight engineer, a tall single fin for low-level stability, unsupercharged engines and rearranged turrets; 739 were built and served from late 1944 until 1954. In the game it is slower than the Liberator and loses power with height, forcing lower and riskier bombing runs. Fourteen Brownings guard the upper half, but the rear and especially the underside are poorly covered. Its strength is a load of eight Type A mines, each as powerful as a 1,000 kg bomb, enough for several bases; it arrived in Update 1.69 "Regia Aeronautica".
pb4y-2_china: The Nationalist air force adopted the PB4Y-2 to make up for its dwindling B-24 fleet and flew it over the mainland well into the 1950s, losing several, one of them to a Burmese Sea Fury, before retiring the type in the early 1960s. Added in Update 1.91 "Night Vision", it shares the usual four-engined bomber traits of sluggish handling and low speed, struggling to reach 400 km/h in level flight, so nearly any fighter can catch it.
pb4y-2_france: France received 22 Privateers under the 1949 Mutual Defense Assistance Act and flew them as bombers in Indochina until the defeat at Dien Bien Phu, after which six went back to the US and the rest moved to North Africa for service in Algeria and the Suez Crisis, before being scrapped in the early 1960s. Added in Update 1.73 "Vive la France", it matches the American and Chinese PB4Y-2s: very slow in level flight for a bomber, but well protected by nose, twin dorsal, twin beam and tail turrets.
pbj_1h: The PBJ-1H was the Navy's B-25 variant, flown by the US Marine Corps as a ground-attack gunship with a 75 mm T13E1 cannon, akin to the Sherman's M3, and eight 12.7 mm guns. With armour-piercing belts the cannon knocks out pillboxes and even light and medium tanks more precisely than bombs, if slowly, leaving soft targets to the machine guns. It keeps the B-25's sluggish handling and big silhouette, with gunner blind spots behind the twin fins and no ventral cover, so escorts and low flying help. It has fewer bombs than the B-25, spawns lower and lacks a bombsight view; it arrived in Update 1.41.
pbj_1j: Navy PBJ Mitchells came from a 1942 deal in which the Navy dropped its XPBB Sea Ranger flying boat and its plant to free capacity for the B-29, receiving 202 B-25s and a Kansas factory in return; the Marine Corps then adopted them, and the PBJ-1J, based on the B-25J, traded the nose gunner for extra Brownings and a radar to reach twelve guns. It flies like the B-25J but, being classed as a strike aircraft, starts much lower. That forward battery shreds aircraft and unarmoured vehicles in its path, yet stiff handling largely confines it to close support. It arrived in Update 1.41.
pbm_1: Glenn L. Martin's PBM Mariner was a gull-winged, twin-tailed flying boat with two 1,600 hp Wright R-2600 engines, entering service in 1940 for patrol and anti-submarine work; Mariners sank ten U-boats, among them U-158 near Bermuda, and the last US squadron gave them up in 1956. In the game it carries a heavy bomb load and five turrets of 12.7 mm guns, unusually strong protection for its level, though its size and weight make it an easy target. None of the turrets covers the underside, so fighters climbing from below call for evasive manoeuvres. It arrived in Update "Hot Tracks".
pbm_3: Martin's PBM-1 Mariner was meant to replace the Catalina but cost more without performing much better, so the PBM-3 received stronger engines, larger fixed floats in place of retractable ones, revised bomb bays and a longer fuselage for steadiness in the air and on the water; only 32 were ordered in 1943, and Mariners served until the P5M Marlin replaced them in the early 1950s. A reward from the 2019 "Sea Voyage" event, it carries a large bomb load, including plenty of naval mines, and takes damage well. It is big and slow, however, and its defensive guns are weak.
pbm_5a: With the R-3350 engines it wanted reserved for the B-29, Martin used R-2800s instead for the PBM-5, the most numerous Mariner at 614 built, and the PBM-5A amphibian added retractable landing gear; about 40 were completed, serving the US Navy until 1956 and the Dutch navy until crashes and technical trouble ended its use in 1959. A reward in Battle Pass Season XVI, "Skilled Marksman", it gains an AN/APS-31 radar over the PBM-3 for finding ground and sea targets. It is slow and its turrets leave the belly uncovered, but it carries a big bomb load, survives well and mounts several turrets of 12.7 mm Brownings.
pby-5: Despite pre-war claims that slow flying boats were finished, the Catalina won the US Navy over with its range, toughness and payload, becoming one of the war's most widely built seaplanes for scouting and U-boat hunting; some still fly as civil aircraft. In the game its large payload can carpet-bomb ground targets, take out several bases or sink ships, a single torpedo being enough for anything short of a carrier. It is slow to accelerate and slow overall, and its 12.7 mm waist guns and 7.62 mm elsewhere can see off a lone biplane but not a group. It dates from the open beta.
pby-5a: Consolidated's answer to a 1933 Navy call for a long-range patrol flying boat became the PBY, the "Y" denoting the maker; the PBY-5A amphibian had two 1,200 hp R-1830-92 engines and a range above 4,000 km, and it served in patrol, rescue and anti-submarine roles, including night work by the black-painted "Black Cats" in the Pacific. In the game it is very slow and its wings tear off in hard turns, but it has plenty of defensive guns and enough bombs to destroy bases, and retractable wheels let it land on runways as well as water. It has been in the game since the open beta.
pby-5a_late_france: France ordered 30 PBY-5s early in the war but surrendered before any arrived; it later obtained three PBY-5As from the Royal Canadian Air Force for its Caribbean territories, which lacked proper airfields, and used them unarmed, mostly to carry passengers. Added in Update "La Royale", the in-game version flies like the American PBY-5A, trading speed, agility and toughness for a very large bomb load. That versatility makes it useful in air, ground and naval battles alike, whether carpet-bombing vehicles, destroying bases or launching torpedoes at ships.
pby-5a_raf: The Catalina joined RAF Coastal Command in 1941 and became a feared U-boat hunter; the Mk IIIa was Britain's name for the amphibious PBY-5A, with 1,200 hp Twin Wasps and retractable landing gear. Added in Update 1.43 as the Catalina Mk IVa and renamed in Update 1.57 "Battle March", it can use runways thanks to its wheels. Large and slow like other bombers at its level, it has guns covering most angles, though they need a trained crew or manual aiming to be effective. Up to 4,000 lb of ordnance, as two torpedoes, four 1,000 lb bombs or four naval mines, threatens ground targets and early destroyers.
pby-5a_ussr: The Soviet Union received 185 Lend-Lease Catalinas from 1944 and relied on them as its main maritime reconnaissance aircraft and naval bomber until 1954-1957; even the Be-6 never fully replaced them. In the game it is best flown high like a heavy bomber, yawing to bring a waist gun to bear, ideally aimed manually as AI gunners are poor at range. It is slow and clumsy, and turning too hard at speed can snap a wing, but its heavy payload and strong defensive armament make it worthwhile. Landing gear eases landings and lets it capture airfields in Arcade's Airfield Domination mode; it is an open-beta original.
pe-2-1: The Pe-2-1 is a fast Soviet dive bomber that fills a similar role to the Il-2 but carries far heavier bombs, often destroying with one bomb what a Sturmovik needs two or three for. Starting at bomber altitude with forward guns, it works well in hit-and-run attacks and finds its niche as a precise dive bomber in tank battles. Its two nose machine guns are weak and short of ammunition, single 7.62 mm guns guard each hemisphere, and a dorsal fuel tank invites diving attacks, so speed, agility and friendly cover are its real protection. Better-armed Pe-2s follow it in the tree, and it dates from the open beta.
pe-2-110: The Pe-2-110 is a Soviet dive bomber with heavier forward firepower than the earliest Pe-2s, including a 12.7 mm UB that, well aimed, can knock out tanks and light pillboxes. Like other Peshkas it takes the Il-2's attack role with much bigger bombs, and its bomber-altitude start and nose guns suit quick strikes. Only one or two defensive guns can engage an attacker at a time, enough to discourage a slow approach from behind but rarely to stop a fighter, and the dorsal fuel tank is vulnerable from above, so speed and friendly cover are its best defence. It has been in the game since the open beta.
pe-2-205: The Pe-2-205 premium, first sold as a "Peshka" starter pack in 2012, is one of the fastest bombers at its level and agile for a twin, relying on that to avoid interception rather than on its gunners, whose rear 12.7 mm UBT is useful but whose waist ShKAS guns are not. Its 1,000 kg bomb load hangs externally and costs performance, but unusually for a bomber at its level it also takes RS-132 rockets, which can be air-burst against bombers, and semi-armour-piercing RBS-132s for tanks. Dive brakes and a level bombsight let it strike pillboxes and tanks precisely, though heavier bombers such as the He 111 do level bombing better.
pe-2-31: After 1941 complaints about weak guns, 12.7 mm UBs began replacing some ShKAS, and the 31 series of summer 1941 to spring 1942 was the first major redesign, identifiable by a triangular nose window on the right that gave mechanics easier access to the guns. In the game it is fast and agile with a very high structural speed limit, but it is a large target with thin armour and weak defensive guns, as only the pilot and one gunner are protected. Compared with the first Pe-2 series it has stronger guns, armour for one gunner and unguided rockets. It dates from the open beta.
pe-2-359: After the 205 series, the Pe-2 gained a long run of small improvements, from extra bomb racks and new propellers to better radios, winterised engine systems and streamlined rack fairings; the 359 series, built from summer 1944, added individual exhaust stacks, minor engine changes and an improved oxygen system. In the game it is a fast, agile dive bomber with a very high structural speed limit, but its forward and defensive guns are weak and it is a large target. Apart from small visual details and the opposition it faces, it is the same aircraft as the Pe-2-205, and it dates from the open beta.
pe-2-83: Like the other Peshkas, the Pe-2-83 is quicker than the Il-2 and carries much heavier bombs, destroying in one drop what a Sturmovik would need several bombs for. Rockets, nose guns and a high Arcade start even let it hunt bombers in a pinch, though its two forward machine guns lack punch and ammunition. Above and below it is covered by just one 7.62 mm gun each, and a dorsal fuel tank is exposed to diving attacks, so it relies on speed, agility and friendly fighters or AA to escape. Its true calling is precise dive bombing in tank battles; it has been in the game since the open beta.
pe-3: Built from the Pe-2 as a heavy night fighter when German night raids began in 1941, the Pe-3 struggled in that role, its pilots dazzled by searchlights and their own gun flashes, and as a day attacker its weak frontal protection cost around a quarter of the first aircraft before most were moved to reconnaissance. In the game it is one of the earliest Soviet strike fighters, with useful light rockets and bombs but disappointing flight performance from low engine power and limited agility. Even so, it is forgiving in mixed battles, prepares pilots for the aircraft that follow and has been in the game since the open beta.
pe-3_bis: The Pe-3bis, the last of the Pe-3 family, shares its relatives' traits and has been in the game since the open beta. A wide choice of rockets and bombs makes it an effective ground attacker, while an air spawn and strong forward-firing guns let it intercept bombers and defend against air attacks. That combination makes it a useful multirole aircraft in both air and mixed battles.
pe-3_early: The Pe-2 itself began as the VI-100 high-altitude fighter, designed from 1938 by imprisoned engineers under V. M. Petlyakov before being turned into a dive bomber; when war came, Petlyakov was given four days in August 1941 to turn the Pe-2 back into a fighter, adding fuel tanks, removing the bomb gear and lower gunner and fitting a second UB machine gun. In the game this early Pe-3 is a heavy fighter that rolls and turns well for a twin, but its armament is weak and its ammunition short, and its many fuel tanks catch fire easily. It has been in the game since the open beta.
pe-8_m82: The Pe-8, which debuted in 1936, was the only four-engined bomber the Soviet Union built during the war; made in small numbers, it flew symbolic long-range raids to lift morale, including attacks on Berlin in 1941, as well as night strikes on factories, airfields and rail yards, before leaving bomber service in 1944 for transport and Arctic work. In the game its nose, tail and dorsal gunners plus two rearward-firing wing positions make attacking it from behind a bad idea. Loads range from 40 small bombs to six 500 kg bombs or a single 5,000 kg FAB-5000, enough for bases, battleships or massed vehicles. It arrived in Update 1.53 "Firestorm".
po-2: Polikarpov's Po-2, the U-2 until 1944, was a 1928 trainer and utility biplane built in 20,000 to 30,000 examples, and its Po-2VS night bomber version, gliding quietly onto targets, was flown most famously by the all-female "Night Witches"; in 1953 one even caused an American F-94 to stall and crash. In the game it is notorious, earning the nickname "2-OP" for its very low top speed and dive limit. It still carries a useful bomb load and can be maddeningly hard to hit thanks to its slow speed and agility, but its flimsy structure gives way to even rifle-calibre fire. It has been in the game since the open beta.
po-2m: The Po-2M, or Po-2P, was a floatplane version of the Po-2 tested successfully on the Khimki reservoir near Moscow, using a single central float so that bombs could still hang under the lower wings; it was never produced, probably because biplanes had fallen out of favour. It was a reward from the 2022 Project "Overpowered" event in Update "Drone Age". It flies like the Po-2 and is still the slowest aircraft in the game, but its payload is strong: it gives up two 50 kg bombs for four extra rockets of each type and gains incendiary bombs, and its defensive gun is a 7.62 mm DA.
potez_630: The Potez 630 was a late-1930s French heavy fighter intended as an answer to the Bf 110, but it proved too slow and clumsy in 1940 and afterwards under Vichy, ending up in second-line duties. In the game it is a sluggish climber that should operate at low to medium altitude, diving on targets below rather than climbing at them. Energy drains after pulling out, faster still in turns and loops, so each pass should flow straight into a climb for the next, turning away to climb if caught low and slow. It arrived in Update 1.73 "Vive la France".
potez_631: The Potez 631 was the second production model of the Potez 63 family, a 1934 heavy-fighter concept that grew into fighters, light bombers, attack and reconnaissance aircraft, with over 1,100 built by June 1940 and some 250 more under German occupation. In the game it pairs two 20 mm nose cannons with six 7.5 mm wing guns, heavy firepower for its rank, but the weight, weaker engines than the Potez 630 and an unremarkable airframe make it a poor duellist. It does best playing a patient boom-and-zoom game away from the busy centre of the map. It came with the original French tree in Update 1.73 "Vive la France".
potez_633: The Potez 633, the two-seat light bomber of the Potez 63 family, was, like its fighter siblings, too slow to survive enemy air superiority in 1940; export orders from China, Romania and Greece were cut short by a French arms embargo in June 1939. In the game it swaps the fighters' cannons and extra guns for a single 7.5 mm nose gun and carries 400 kg of bombs, the pair of 200 kg bombs being the better option and able to deal with light tanks. Being slow and big, it is especially vulnerable to SPAA. It arrived in Update 1.73 "Vive la France".
pv_2d: The Harpoon developed Lockheed's PV-1 Ventura for maritime work, with a longer wing to cure poor take-off performance, more fuel and no bombardier's station; early wings wrinkled in testing and had to be redesigned, after which it proved popular in US service and with Brazil and New Zealand. A rare reward from the 2017 World War Two: Chronicle event in Update 1.67 "Assault", the PV-2D outclasses the B-34 with a bigger bomb load, more defensive guns and eight forward-firing 12.7 mm guns, whose belts are mostly incendiary even without late-war options. Starting at bomber altitude, it can bomb first and then hunt aircraft, and its flaps let it turn surprisingly tightly.
pyorremyrsky: Expecting Bf 109 deliveries to dry up, Finland asked VL for a fighter of domestic wood and steel to match the Bf 109 G-6; the Pyörremyrsky ("hurricane") used a DB 605AC and the Messerschmitt's spinner and cowling, giving it a familiar nose. In the game it sits between turn fighters like the Yak-3 and energy fighters like the Bf 109, climbing like the latter while matching Soviet fighters for speed and agility. Ammunition is limited and Zeros, Spitfires and C.205s out-fly it, so patient attacks on slower aircraft work best. First a premium pack in Update 1.93 "Shark Attack", it returned as an in-game premium in "Fire and Ice".
q_5_early: The Q-5 grew from the PLAAF's wish for a jet successor to the Il-10, which had impressed during the capture of Nationalist-held islands: a MiG-19 derivative with side intakes, it took a decade to develop amid the Great Leap Forward's economic troubles, entering service in 1969, with 515 built by 1979. Added in Update "Raining Fire", it was China's first supersonic striker and the first home-grown jet in its tree. It outdoes the J-6A on the ground with up to four 250 kg bombs and 90 mm rocket pods, and its similar handling and guns make it a capable fighter too, though it is demanding to fly.
q_5a: The Q-5A, called Q-5I until 1987, answered a 1976 PLAAF request for more combat radius with extra internal fuel, new engines and other refinements, and after tests in 1979-80 it was certified in 1983 as the main production model, later gaining a radar warning receiver, countermeasures and new sights in the Q-5IA standard. In the game it looks like the early Q-5 apart from an all-white finish, but adds flares, an RWR, a ballistic computer and extra hardpoints for 130 mm rockets. Its stronger engines noticeably improve flight performance, making it better than its predecessor both at defending itself and at hitting ground targets. It arrived in Update "New Power".
q_5l: Unable to buy foreign targeting pods, China developed its own laser-guided bombs and pods in the 1990s, and the early-2000s Q-5L upgrade let a single Q-5 use them, remaining standard until retirement in the early 2010s. In the game it adds a larger bomb load and a FLIR under the nose, but with no air-to-air missiles it is no better a fighter than the Q-5A and remains fragile. Laser-guided bombs and a thermal targeting pod, which arrive much earlier than on the Jaguar GR.1A or Mirage 2000D-R1, make up for that and let it pick off vehicles with little worry about air defences.
quing_6: China bought six Soviet Be-6 flying boats in 1955 for naval patrol from Qingdao, and when spares for their piston engines ran short in the 1970s it re-engined them with WJ-6 turboprops as the Qing-6, which served until the SH-5 replaced it in 1986. In the game the turboprops add little top speed but greatly improve acceleration and energy retention over the Be-6. Its Chinese bombs carry less explosive than Soviet ones, but napalm bombs can wipe out several bases. Five 23 mm cannons give strong protection, though the underside is a large blind spot that attackers will exploit; it arrived in Update "Tusk Force".
r2y2_kai: Yokosuka's Keiun began as a fast reconnaissance aircraft; after the piston R2Y1 flew in May 1945, a jet bomber version with two Ne-330 turbojets was proposed, but a raid destroyed the sole prototype days later. The V3 is a hypothetical version styled after Korean War-era jets, its large nose intake bringing extra thrust. Big but surprisingly agile, it downs fighters with slow-firing, hard-hitting cannons, though it gathers speed slowly and must not waste energy. An 800 kg bomb and cannons that pierce light vehicles serve for ground attack; it arrived in Update 1.43.
r2y2_v1: The R2Y2 Keiun Kai was a proposed jet light bomber derived from Yokosuka's R2Y1 reconnaissance aircraft, which flew only in May 1945 before the sole prototype was destroyed in a raid; the jet version would have used two Ne-330 turbojets and carried up to 800 kg of bombs. The V1 represents that original layout, with the engines slung beneath the wings. Large yet more agile than it looks, it can kill any fighter with its hard-hitting, low-rate-of-fire cannons given good aim and energy, though it builds speed slowly and should not overcommit. An 800 kg bomb and cannons able to pierce light vehicles handle ground targets; it arrived in Update 1.43.
r2y2_v2: Like the other Keiun Kai variants, the V2 is based on the R2Y2, a jet light-bomber conversion of Yokosuka's R2Y1 reconnaissance aircraft that was proposed in May 1945 and dropped when the only prototype was bombed. This version imagines a dedicated fighter-bomber layout, its rear-mounted engines breathing through wing intakes to cut drag. Bulky but agile for an early jet, it hits hard with slow-firing cannons yet accelerates slowly, so energy must be guarded and over-extending avoided. It can also drop an 800 kg bomb on ground targets and penetrate light vehicles with its guns; it arrived in Update 1.43.
rafale_c_f3: France left the multinational project that became the Eurofighter Typhoon in 1985, and Dassault pressed on alone, flying the first Rafale in 1986 and putting it into Air Force service in 2005; the F3 upgrade brought a new radar, better communications and sensors, the DAMOCLES pod and weapons such as the AASM HAMMER. In the game the canard-delta layout makes it very responsive in tight turns, and strong engines recover lost energy quickly. MICA-EM radar missiles and multi-mode HAMMER bombs give it reach in the air and on the ground, but it carries only a few Magic 2s and has a small flare supply. It arrived in Update 2.43 "Storm Warning".
rafale_eg_greece: Greece ordered 18 Rafales in January 2021, six new and 12 from French service, to replace its Mirage 2000EG/BGs, then added six more; the first reached Tanagra in January 2022, the type entered service in September 2023 and the last of the 24 arrived in January 2025. In the Israeli tree its canards and delta wing keep it controllable at high angles of attack, and its twin engines quickly rebuild speed after hard manoeuvres. MICA-EM missiles cover air combat and AASM HAMMER bombs with inertial, satellite, laser or infrared guidance handle ground targets, though Magic 2s and countermeasures are scarce. It came in Update 2.59 "Sky Odyssey".
rafale_m_f3r: The navalised Rafale M added a strengthened structure and undercarriage, an arrestor hook and a built-in ladder; it flew in 1991, was combat-ready by 2004, and 42 now serve the French Navy in upgraded F3-R form. In the game it is among the best-handling jets available, rivalled mainly by the Eurofighter Typhoon: it turns well at any speed, holds energy, accelerates hard and is very fast. Magic 2 and MICA-EM missiles and a broad range of ground-attack weapons complete the package, although it is heavier than the Rafale C and its cannon is awkward to use with little ammunition. It arrived in Update 2.53 "Line of Contact".
rah_66: Designed to replace the Army's OH-6 and OH-58 with the emphasis on low radar, noise and heat signatures, the Comanche first flew in 1996, but rising costs, ageing technology and a shift to counter-terrorism ended it in 2004 after two were built. In the game radar barely sees it and heat-seekers lock on only at very close range, so it can launch missiles almost unseen, and its own radar spots air and ground targets. Its Hellfires need the target kept in view, exposing it to fast SAMs, and lacking flares or chaff it must use agility and terrain; Stingers and a 20 mm cannon handle aircraft. It arrived in Update 2.47 "Leviathans".
re_2000_ga: The Re.2000 G.A. ("Grande Autonomia") was a long-range version meant to fly directly from Italy to Ethiopia in 1941, when Italian forces there were outmatched, with extra wing tanks, a Piaggio P.XI adapted for African conditions and underwing bomb racks; East Africa fell before it arrived, and some later became catapult fighters as the Serie III. In the game it is a nimble early monoplane with two 12.7 mm Breda-SAFAT guns and two 100 kg bombs that can kill even heavy armour if dropped accurately. The engine overheats quickly, though, and the extra fuel adds weight and blunts an already mediocre climb. It arrived in Update 1.79 "Project X".
re_2000_heja_1: Hungary bought Re.2000s from Italy in 1939, along with a production licence, and upgraded the imported aircraft with an 8 mm armour plate, an extra fuel tank and other small changes as the Héja I ("Hawk"); at least one squadron fought on the Eastern Front before Bf 109s replaced it. In the Italian tree that plate, weighing almost 150 kg, shields the pilot from behind against rifle-calibre and some heavy machine-gun fire at the cost of extra weight. Otherwise it matches the Re.2000 minus some engine power: brisk for an early fighter, with a pair of 12.7 mm Bredas, though it climbs only modestly. It arrived in Update 2.55 "Ninth Wave".
re_2000_heja_2: The Héja II was Hungary's deeper rework of the Re.2000: Gebauer 1940 M GKM 12.7 mm guns replaced the Breda-SAFATs, curing their synchronisation problems, and a more reliable WM K-14B engine, a new propeller and smaller wing tanks were fitted; 204 were built up to August 1944 for interceptor and training duties. In the Italian tree it is a fast early fighter, agile for a monoplane and fairly well armed, with more engine power than the Héja I, although its climb rate is still only average. It arrived in Update 2.55 "Ninth Wave".
re_2000_int: Inspired by the Seversky P-35, Reggiane's mid-1930s Re.2000 out-turned the Macchi C.200 and Bf 109 E in trials, yet the Regia Aeronautica was unimpressed, so most went to Sweden and Hungary, and the design fathered the Re.2001 to Re.2005. In the game it is a strong dogfighter that accelerates well and climbs better than many early fighters, early Bf 109s included. It suits both energy and turning fights, and climbing to around 3,000-4,000 m early, then diving on targets, gives it the initiative. Spitfires and I-16s are the threats to watch, out-turning it without a biplane's loss of speed; it arrived in Update 1.77 "Advancing Storm".
re_2000_j20: Cut off from American aircraft when the US halted military exports, Sweden bought 60 Re.2000s as the J20; despite an unreliable engine, pilots liked its handling, and with wing F 10 at Malmö it intercepted intruders into neutral airspace, one being lost in 1945 while intercepting a German Do 24. In the game it is identical to the Italian Re.2000 serie 1, with an outstanding climb and a short turn time that suit both energy and turning fights. Its weaknesses are a light armament of two 12.7 mm guns and compression from about 400 km/h, and full manual engine control is there for experts. It arrived in Update 1.95 "Northern Wind".
re_2001_cb: Reggiane's Re.2001 replaced the Re.2000's troublesome radial with the Alfa Romeo RA1000, a licence-built DB 601, and added two more 7.7 mm guns; the CB fighter-bomber version, of which 39 were built in 1942-43, gained racks for bombs from 50 to 630 kg and fought both ground targets and Allied aircraft. In the game its 250 kg and 630 kg bombs can destroy heavy tanks, the smaller ones only soft targets. Armour plate and bulletproof glass give the pilot a slightly better chance in head-on passes, and otherwise it flies like the first series, out-fighting most monoplanes as long as the quick-to-overheat engine is watched. It arrived in Update 1.85 "Supersonic".
re_2001_cn: The Re.2001 CN was the night-fighter version of Reggiane's DB 601-powered fighter, with exhaust flame dampers, dark camouflage, a fuselage bomb rack and, on most aircraft, 20 mm MG 151 cannons in place of the wing machine guns; 94 were built in 1942-43. In the game those cannons make short work of anything from fighters to heavy bombers and armoured attackers, though with only 60 rounds per gun each burst must count. A 250 kg bomb lets it take on tanks in mixed battles, and it dogfights as well as other Re.2001s, provided the engine is kept from overheating. It arrived in Update 1.85 "Supersonic".
re_2001_serie1: Added in Update 1.85 "Supersonic", the Re.2001 serie 1 plays much like the Macchi C.202. It turns noticeably better, with an upgraded turn time of about 18 seconds against the C.202's 21.4, but it is slower, climbs worse, has less armour, an engine that overheats sooner and landing gear that takes longer to cycle. Tactics suited to the C.202 work here too, with extra care given its thinner protection.
re_2001_serie1_ep: This premium Re.2001 carries the markings of the 22° Gruppo, a fighter group formed in 1918 that fought in the First World War and, in the Second, on the Eastern Front and over the Mediterranean, where it received its first Re.2001s; after the war it became an interceptor group within the 51° Stormo. Added in Update "Starfighters", it is very nimble but not especially fast, and combat flaps sharpen its turn further at a heavy cost in speed. It needs WEP to perform, yet poor cooling means extended use overheats and can damage the engine. Its mixed battery of 12.7 mm and 7.7 mm guns does real damage when aimed well.
re_2002_early: The Re.2002 "Ariete II" adapted the Re.2001 for attack and support work with a Piaggio P.XIX radial, better at low level and tougher than the DB 601A, plus a cooling fan and a heavier bomb pylon; despite a temperamental engine and poor view it proved versatile, though delays meant it reached units late, and after Italy's surrender a plan to finish the last 56 with BMW 801s failed because the engine would not fit. In the game it is a capable fighter-bomber, agile and tough-engined, with two heavy machine guns and external stores, but it is slow, lightly armoured and prone to catching fire. It arrived in Update 1.89 "Imperial Navy".
re_2005_serie0: The Re.2005 "Sagittario" was the final refinement of Reggiane's Re.2000 line, a sleek DB 605A-powered fighter capable of well over 640 km/h whose elliptical wing let it turn with Spitfires; German pilots likened it to the Bf 109 G-14, but only a handful were built. In the game it meets much faster opponents such as the F8F Bearcat and Griffon Spitfires, so it must expect diving attacks, reversing onto enemies after their passes or side-climbing until they lose height. Three MG 151 cannons and two 12.7 mm Bredas with ample ammunition destroy aircraft quickly, but it is a hard aircraft to do well in. It arrived in Update 1.91 "Night Vision".
re_2005_vdm: The second Re.2005 prototype, MM.495, first flew in October 1942 and in 1943 was fitted with a German VDM propeller and a DB605AM engine, flying in that form under German supervision in June before trials at Rechlin, after which its fate is unknown; of 750 Re.2005s ordered, only 48 production aircraft were completed. A reward in Battle Pass Season XXI, "Brave Archer", it has a stronger engine than the Re.2005 serie 0 but is otherwise the same, combining good guns and bomb options with decent speed and excellent agility. Faster jets can still give it trouble.
ro_43: IMAM's Ro.43 adapted the proven Ro.37 "Lince" for shipboard reconnaissance, with a central float holding its fuel, wingtip floats and folding wings for catapults squeezed between a ship's superstructure; about 130 were built from 1936, and one crew's sighting of the British fleet preceded the Italian defeat at Cape Matapan. In the game it is carried only by certain Italian bluewater ships and is one of the fastest, nimblest seaplanes available. With just two 7.7 mm Bredas and a turret behind the cockpit, it is best used to capture distant points, scout for enemy ships and lay smoke screens. It arrived in Update 2.13 "Winged Lions".
ro_44: The Ro.44 was IMAM's single-seat fighter version of the Ro.43, first flown in October 1936, with two 12.7 mm Breda-SAFAT guns in the nose and a reworked rear fuselage and tail; it inherited the Ro.43's poor buoyancy and handling on the water, and only 35 of 51 ordered were built, serving with 161 Squadriglia in the Aegean before going to seaplane schools early in the war. Added in Update "Sky Guardians", it completed the set of seaplanes available to every naval nation. Its value lies in capturing naval points, as reserve biplanes such as the He 51 and I-15 are both faster and more agile.
ro_57_quadriarma: IMAM's Ro.57 twin-engined fighter of 1939 was quicker than Italy's single-engined fighters but otherwise mediocre and was rejected, so it became the Ro.57 bis "Quadriarma" attack aircraft, gaining bomb racks, air brakes and a pair of 20 mm cannons; it flew even worse, but the Breda Ba.88's failure led to an order, and 75 were assembled, none seeing action. A reward from the 2020 "Operation W.I.N.T.E.R" event, it is slower and climbs worse than other twin-engined fighters yet turns with some single-engined ones. Limited ammunition and unimpressive machine guns hamper it in the air, but bombs of up to 500 kg make it useful against ground targets.
s_199: After the war Avia kept building Bf 109s in Czechoslovakia, but with no suitable engines left it fitted the Jumo 211F bomber engine, creating the S-199; Israel bought 25, which arrived as the 1948 war began, and despite failing engines, jamming guns and even shot-off propellers they downed several Egyptian aircraft early on. In the game the "Sakeen" is underpowered, accelerates poorly and handles badly, but its upgraded guns destroy most opponents in a few bursts. It works best as a support fighter, climbing high or lurking on the flanks before diving on enemies below and hoarding every bit of speed. It came with the Israeli tree in Update "Winged Lions".
s_81_ar125: Alessandro Marchetti derived the S.81 "Pipistrello" ("Bat") from the SM.73 airliner to give Italy a long-ranged bomber and reconnaissance aircraft for Africa; first flown in 1935, it fought in Spain and Africa, and 534 were built, but it was dated by 1939. In the game its three engines are individually weak, so losing one costs a lot of speed and height, though the nose engine adds some resilience. Dorsal, ventral and two beam positions give good, overlapping fields of fire, but only with 7.7 mm guns, and with no armour the crew is easily wounded, especially from below. It arrived in Update 1.71 "New E.R.A.".
sa_313b: Sud-Aviation's Alouette II light helicopter was built in more than 1,000 examples for civil and military users, about 220 of them for West Germany, which added its own weapons, MG3 machine guns two to a landing skid and SS.11 anti-tank missiles on fuselage crossbeams, and kept them until the mid-2000s. In the game it is light, quick and agile, able to support ground forces and then get away fast when threatened by air defences. It takes practice to fly well, and with no armour and only modest weapons it cannot afford to be caught. It arrived in Update 1.83 "Masters of the Sea".
sa_313b_france: The Alouette II first flew in 1955 with a Turbomeca Artouste turbine, setting altitude records, and the SE 313B version's 400 hp Artouste II raised maximum take-off weight to 1,600 kg; built successively by Sud-Est, Sud-Aviation and Aérospatiale, it was a small helicopter with an excellent view, flown for scouting and training. In the game it has anti-tank missiles from the start, which makes upgrading it easier than most early helicopters, but its four missiles are slow and sluggish, backed only by four 7.62 mm machine guns. With no armour, even roof-mounted machine guns can hit its crew and vital parts. It arrived in Update 1.87 "Locked On".
sa_316b: The larger Alouette III flew in 1959 and became a trusted transport and rescue helicopter, strong at altitude, reliable and cheap; armed versions carried machine guns, 20 mm cannon, SS.11 missiles, torpedoes or rockets, and the 1968 SA 316B brought tougher rotor blades. In the game it is slow, sluggish and large, easy prey for SPAA, so it suits experienced helicopter pilots. Its SS.11 missiles have decent range, and without thermal sights it relies on cover, rising from behind hills and trees to fire, ideally at targets teammates or a scout drone have marked. It arrived in Update 1.87 "Locked On".
sa_341f: Sud Aviation began the Gazelle in 1966 to replace the French Army's Alouette II, and the SA.341 introduced its enclosed "fenestron" tail rotor; the armed SA.341F, with an uprated engine and options for a 20 mm cannon, HOT-2 anti-tank missiles and Mistral air-to-air missiles, followed the type's 1973 adoption, with about 150 built by 1996. In the game its loadout sets its role: missiles or rockets for tanks, Mistrals and the cannon for aircraft and helicopters. Small, light, fast and agile, it strikes quickly and dodges ground fire well, but with no radar warning receiver and little armour it must rely on staying hidden. It arrived in Update 1.87 "Locked On".
sa_342l_china: With no suitable attack helicopter of its own while planning an army aviation corps, the PLA bought eight SA.342L Gazelles with HOT missiles from Aérospatiale in the late 1980s, making them its first armed helicopters; they served as scouts and missile testbeds, often playing the enemy in exercises, and probably now train pilots. In the game it has neither armour nor countermeasures nor air-to-air missiles, so quick, nimble flying is what keeps it alive, while a small but useful mix of anti-tank missiles, two rocket pods and machine-gun pods lets it fight back. It arrived in Update "Drone Age".
sa_342m: The SA.342M was the French Army's improved Gazelle, entering service in 1984 with a stronger engine, better optics and avionics and extra pylons that doubled its payload; it flew in the Gulf War among other conflicts and is now being phased out. In the game it drops the SA.341F's 20 mm cannon but gains a second ordnance pylon and a thermal imager for spotting targets. Otherwise it is the same quick, agile Gazelle, good at fast hit-and-run strikes but fragile. It arrived in Update 1.87 "Locked On".
saab_105g: The Saab 105 entered Swedish service in 1967 as a jet trainer that could also attack and scout, replacing the Vampire; the single 105G was a development of the J85-powered 105XT export demonstrator with new avionics, a precision navigation and attack system and a modified wing. In the game it is close to the Austrian Saab 105OE but carries free-fall bombs and unguided rockets instead of Rb05A guided missiles. It is nimble but slow and accelerates poorly. It arrived in Update "Hot Tracks".
saab_105oe: Austria took 40 Saab 105OEs, a development of the J85-powered 105XT, from July 1970 to replace its Saab 29 Tunnans and Vampires, and flew them for half a century until retiring the last on 31 December 2020. Compared with the Swedish 105G in the game, it lacks that aircraft's modified wing and slightly more powerful J85s, and it cannot carry bombs, though it gains Rb05A guided missiles that the 105G does not have. Like its sibling it is agile but slow, with sluggish acceleration. It arrived in Update "Hot Tracks".
saab_a21a_3: Saab's pusher-propeller 21 was proposed by Fred Wanström to simplify gun installation and ease take-off and landing; developed from 1941, it entered production in 1945, and the A21A-3 of 1947 added mounts for bombs and drop tanks to replace the outdated B17 and B5 in the attack role, serving until 1954. In the game the layout allows a heavy nose armament and a good view from the cockpit, but the engine overheats and overall flight performance is poor. Unusually for a piston aircraft, it also has a ballistic computer to help with ground attack. It arrived in Update 1.95 "Northern Wind".
saab_a21rb: Rather than pursue an improved piston J21B, Saab and the Swedish Air Force turned to jets after the war and found it simplest to fit a British Goblin engine into the existing Saab 21 airframe; the J21R prototypes flew in 1947, and the A21RB attack version with the stronger Goblin III followed, with 30 built from 1950, none seeing combat. In the game it is agile and well armed, but its engine is weak and its speed limit low. It arrived in Update 1.95 "Northern Wind".
saab_a32a: Saab's Lansen, first flown in 1952 with a licence-built Rolls-Royce Avon, became the first Swedish aircraft to pass the speed of sound, in a dive; the A32A attack version served from 1954 to 1978 without seeing combat. In the game it is slow and clumsy, but ballistic computers for bombs, rockets and guns, plus 600 kg bombs that can level a base, make it a capable attacker. It has no flares or missiles, though two chaff pods help against early radar missiles, and a strong radar, well-stocked cannons and good energy retention let it lure MiG-21s and other deltas into bleeding speed. It arrived in Update 1.95 "Northern Wind".
saab_a32a_red_adam: Conceived in 1948 as a radar-equipped, all-weather attack aircraft able to reach any stretch of Sweden's coast within an hour, the Lansen entered service as the A32A in 1955, with 287 built. This version wears the "Red A" markings of an F 17 Kallinge aircraft from the 1950s and otherwise matches the standard A32A: neither fast nor agile, but its powerful bombs and ballistic computer make it an excellent attacker. In the air it is not helpless, thanks to good energy retention, capable avionics and a quartet of 20 mm cannons, but it carries no countermeasures or air-to-air missiles. It arrived in Update 2.29 "Sons of Attila".
saab_aj37: The AJ37 was the attack version of Saab's Viggen, delivered from mid-1971 with 108 built, carrying RB 04 anti-ship and RB 05 air-to-surface missiles, later the Maverick, along with bombs, rockets and Sidewinders for self-defence. In the game it is far more effective against ground targets than aircraft, its best weapon being the long-range, TV-guided RB75 (AGM-65B Maverick) against armour. For protection it carries two RB24J missiles and external gun pods, but the guns take the slots otherwise used for countermeasures. Heavy and poor at low speed, it should stay fast and turn only when the situation favours it; it arrived in Update "Ground Breaking".
saab_ajs37: The AJS37 came from a 1992 decision to extend the lives of the AJ37, SH37 and SF37 Viggens and give them some of the multirole ability of the JAS 39. Most of the work went into a far more capable central computer, which opened up new weapons: the RB 74 air-to-air missile, the RB 15F for use against ships and BK 90 cluster weapons. It served until 2001, when the Gripen took over, and arrived in the game with Update "La Royale".
saab_ajs37_early: AJS stands for attack, fighter and reconnaissance, reflecting a 1990s upgrade that let attack Viggens also fly reconnaissance; between 1993 and 1998, 48 were modified with two extra pylons, the RB 15F anti-ship missile, capacity for four RB 75s instead of two and BK 90 guided cluster bombs, serving until 2005 without seeing combat. It plays exactly like the later AJS37 in the game, combining a high top speed and thrust reversers with four RB 74s, a Swedish licence-built AIM-9L. It has no internal cannon, limited ground-attack weapons and bleeds energy quickly when manoeuvring. It arrived in Update 2.57 "Heavy Cavalry".
saab_b17a: Begun by ASJA as the L 10 to replace Sweden's Fokker S 6 reconnaissance biplanes and renamed Saab 17 after the 1939 merger, the type served Sweden only briefly before jets arrived but flew abroad for two more decades; the B17A was the most numerous version, 132 built with a Swedish-built Twin Wasp. In the game it is the fastest B17 and a nimble attacker, with a good bomb load: 250 kg and 500 kg bombs for heavier tanks, 50 kg bombs for most AI targets in air battles. Its rear gun will not deter fighters, though, and biplanes out-turn it easily. It arrived in Update 1.95 "Northern Wind".
saab_b17b: The B17B followed the B17A with the main change being a Swedish-built Bristol Mercury XXIV engine, and it later became the basis of the S17BS floatplane. In the game it is reasonably quick, if not faster than most fighters, so diving to low level and heading straight for the target, or swinging wide along the map edges, helps it arrive unnoticed. Its payload suits ground attack: smaller bombs for pillboxes and tank columns in air battles, and 250 kg or 500 kg bombs for player vehicles in ground battles. It arrived in Update 1.95 "Northern Wind".
saab_b17bs: The Saab 17 of 1940 was Sweden's first home-grown all-metal, stressed-skin design, and the S17BS was a reconnaissance version of the B17B with camera equipment, floats in place of wheels and a Bristol Mercury XXIV engine; 38 were built. In the game it is slow and sluggish, with two forward machine guns that are adequate for its level. Its real job is ground attack, dropping nine 50 kg bombs with the help of a bombsight, which makes it effective against light defences and convoys of vehicles in air battles. It arrived in Update "Raining Fire".
saab_b18a: Saab's 18 began as a 1938 requirement for a fast three-seat reconnaissance aircraft to supplement the Ju 86K-based B3C, but was reworked into a medium bomber too, and the changes delayed service until mid-1944; the B18A's twin R-1830 Twin Wasps left it underpowered, a problem later versions solved with licence-built DB 605s. In the game it can bomb vehicles and AA from medium altitude or go after bases, and flying high keeps it clear of most fighters, which tend to stay low. It also works down at low level, and with rockets fitted it can dive on tanks, bunkers, AA guns and ships. It arrived in Update 1.95 "Northern Wind".
saab_b18b: Once the underpowered B18A's Twin Wasps gave way to licence-built DB 605s, the Saab 18 was developed into the B18B dive bomber and ground attacker, carrying three 120 kg bombs or 12 m/51 rockets between its bay and wing hardpoints and serving the Swedish Air Force until 1959. Defence is limited to two 13.2 mm guns in a rear dorsal position with narrow coverage, plus one 13.2 mm gun for the pilot. In the game it can bomb from medium altitude, above most fighters, or attack low down, using rockets to dive on tanks, bunkers, AA and ships. It arrived in Update 1.95 "Northern Wind".
saab_b3c: Junkers developed the Ju 86 in the mid-1930s alongside the He 111, presenting it as a ten-seat airliner that could readily become a bomber at a time when Germany could not openly build them; its diesel engines proved unreliable in Spain, and export Ju 86Ks went to Sweden and Hungary, the Swedish B3C using Bristol Mercury radials. Average in speed, climb and handling, it has bomb options that let it carpet-bomb light targets or hit bases and heavier targets, and an 853 kg torpedo makes it a threat to ships. Several well-placed defensive guns help it reach the target. It arrived in Update 1.95 "Northern Wind".
